title: Today: JMA is still tracking heavy rain and strong winds from the front and Typhoon No. 24
summary: The Japan Meteorological Agency's current disaster-period dataset covers September 2–5 and attributes the ongoing heavy-rain and strong-wind episode to a front and Typhoon No. 24. This is a short-life safety story: conditions and warnings can change by the hour, so the useful source is JMA's live warning and risk maps rather than yesterday's headline.
why_it_matters: Weather stories become dangerous when they remain prominent after conditions change. ALAM should surface this while the event is active, then let it fall away quickly. People in affected areas should rely on current municipal/JMA warnings, especially for flooding, landslide and transport risk.

sources.title: 最新の気象データ — 2026年9月2日～9月5日（前線や令和8年台風第24号に伴う大雨や暴風）

claims.text: JMA is maintaining a special-period dataset for September 2–5, 2026 covering heavy rain and strong winds associated with a front and Typhoon No. 24.
JMA provides live warning/advisory and risk-distribution pages that should be checked for current local conditions.

editorial_visual.scene: a Japan weather map under heavy rain bands with a phone showing a live warning screen
editorial_visual.caption: Use live JMA warnings; this story should age out fast

content.key_message: Check the live JMA warning/risk map for your location before travel or outdoor plans today; do not rely on a static article for rapidly changing weather.
content.who_is_affected: People in areas under or near heavy rain, flood, landslide or strong-wind warnings/advisories, plus anyone traveling through affected corridors.
content.when: Active September 5, 2026. Recheck live conditions because the situation can change within hours.
content.risk_if_ignored: Outdated weather information can understate or overstate actual local risk. Flooding and landslide danger can also remain after the heaviest rain moves away.
content.deadline: Today; reassess before each trip or outdoor activity while warnings remain active.
content.effort: Very low: check JMA warnings and Kikikuru for your municipality/route.
content.potential_benefit: Avoiding unnecessary travel into hazardous conditions or identifying when a route/area is no longer under elevated risk.
content.downside: National-level summaries are intentionally broad; local JMA and municipal information overrides this article.

reading_levels.30 sec: JMA is still tracking the Sep. 2–5 heavy-rain/strong-wind episode tied to a front and Typhoon No. 24. Check the live warning and Kikikuru maps for your location; this is not a story to keep pinned after conditions change.
reading_levels.2 min: JMA's current special-period weather dataset remains active through September 5 for heavy rain and strong winds associated with a front and Typhoon No. 24. The practical point is not to memorize a national forecast: use the live warning/advisory page and Kikikuru risk map for the municipality and route you actually care about. Weather articles should have short shelf lives because both danger and false alarm can result from stale information.

title: September utility support is still active: standard households are getting automatic electricity/gas discounts
summary: Government guidance published September 3 says the July–September electricity and gas support is still being applied automatically. It estimates roughly ¥5,000 of total relief over the three months for a standard household. For September usage, the published discount is ¥3.5/kWh for low-voltage electricity and ¥14.0/m³ for city gas.
why_it_matters: This is small compared with rent or food costs, but it is immediate household cash-flow relief and requires no application. It is also a useful bill-check item: households can verify the discount on their monthly statement instead of assuming a separate cash payment will arrive.

claims.text: Japan's July–September 2026 electricity and gas price support is applied automatically and does not require a household application.
Government guidance estimates about ¥5,000 of total July–September relief for a standard household.
For September usage, the published discount is ¥3.5 per kWh for low-voltage electricity and ¥14.0 per cubic meter for city gas.

editorial_visual.scene: a family using air conditioning while an electricity bill shows an automatic government discount line
editorial_visual.caption: The September discount should appear on the bill automatically

content.key_message: No application is needed; check your electricity/gas statement to confirm the September support is reflected.
content.who_is_affected: Households covered by the national electricity/gas support program, including ordinary low-voltage residential electricity users and eligible city-gas users.
content.when: Support covers July through September 2026 usage; this article focuses on the September portion.
content.financial_impact: Government guidance estimates about ¥5,000 total over July–September for a standard household. Actual savings vary with usage and contract type.
content.risk_if_ignored: Mostly missed awareness rather than lost eligibility because the discount is automatic. The practical risk is misunderstanding the bill or over-cutting cooling use during continued heat because you expect no support.
content.deadline: Check the statement covering September usage when it arrives.
content.potential_benefit: Confirming the automatic discount and understanding the actual household energy-cost reduction.
content.downside: The ¥5,000 figure is a standard-household estimate, not a guaranteed payment to every household.

reading_levels.30 sec: Japan's July–September utility support is still active. No application is needed. September's published residential discount is ¥3.5/kWh for low-voltage electricity and ¥14/m³ for city gas; check the discount on your bill.
reading_levels.2 min: The government is still subsidizing household electricity and gas costs through September. The support is applied through bills rather than as a separate application-based payment. September guidance gives a low-voltage electricity discount of ¥3.5/kWh and a city-gas discount of ¥14/m³, and estimates roughly ¥5,000 of total relief across July–September for a standard household. Actual savings depend on use and contract type, so the best verification is the bill itself.
